title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 210 (Investigation into affairs of company)

content.overview: Section 210 empowers the Central Government to order an investigation into the affairs of a company where it is of the opinion that it is necessary to do so—(a) on the receipt of a report of the Registrar or inspector under section 208; (b) on intimation of a special resolution passed by a company that its affairs ought to be investigated; (c) in public interest; or (d) on request from any Department of the Central Government or a State Government. The Central Government may appoint one or more competent persons as inspectors. The investigation is without prejudice to the SFIO route under section 212. Inspectors have the powers under section 217.
content.glance: CG may order investigation on: s. 208 report; company special resolution; public interest; or government department request; appoints inspectors; distinct from SFIO assignment under s. 212.
content.study: Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary to investigate into the affairs of a company—(a) on the receipt of a report of the Registrar or inspector under section 208; (b) on intimation of a special resolution passed by a company that the affairs of the company ought to be investigated; (c) in public interest; or (d) on request from any Department of the Central Government or a State Government, it may order an investigation into the affairs of the company. The Central Government may appoint one or more competent persons as inspectors to investigate the affairs of the company. Current-law framing: identify one of the four triggers; confirm CG order; note appointment of inspectors and their powers under s. 217; distinguish from SFIO investigation under s. 212 and from Tribunal-ordered investigation under s. 213.

sections.heading: Triggers
sections.body: (a) Report under s. 208; (b) company special resolution that affairs ought to be investigated; (c) public interest; (d) request from a Central or State Government department.

sections.heading: Order and Inspectors
sections.body: Central Government orders investigation and may appoint one or more competent persons as inspectors.

sections.heading: Powers
sections.body: Inspectors exercise the powers provided under section 217 and related provisions.

sections.heading: Relationship to SFIO
sections.body: s. 210 investigation is without prejudice to assignment of a case to SFIO under section 212.

examples.title: Public-interest investigation
examples.body: The Central Government, considering the scale of alleged mismanagement affecting depositors, orders an investigation under s. 210 in public interest and appoints inspectors.

examples.title: Special resolution route
examples.body: Members pass a special resolution that the company’s affairs ought to be investigated. On intimation, the Central Government may order investigation under s. 210(b).

hypotheticals.question: Is a s. 210 investigation the same as an SFIO investigation under s. 212?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 210 is the Central Government’s general power to order investigation and appoint inspectors. Section 212 is the distinct route by which the Central Government assigns investigation of a company’s affairs to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office.

distinctions.title: CG investigation (s. 210) vs SFIO investigation (s. 212)
distinctions.left: CG orders investigation and appoints inspectors on four triggers
distinctions.right: CG assigns case to SFIO; exclusivity and arrest/bail rules apply

misconceptions.trap: Only the Registrar’s report can trigger a Central Government investigation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 210 lists four independent triggers: s. 208 report, company special resolution, public interest, and request from a government department.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 210 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the trigger. II. Confirm CG order and inspectors. III. Note powers under s. 217. IV. Distinguish SFIO/Tribunal routes. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Trigger facts; order status; inspector appointment; precise relief.

examTips: Distinct from SFIO (s. 212) and Tribunal order (s. 213).
